newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB keeps wheat pool prices unchanged.
newsitem.headline: AWB keeps wheat pool prices unchanged.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Tuesday it had kept its wheat pool prices unchanged.
The move surprised the trade, which had been widely expecting a pools price cut of A$5.00-A$10.00 a tonne.
The steady 1996/97 and 1997/98 pool equities reflected stabilised world prices, AWB pricing manager Ruth Horsfall said.

"While world prices declined during May in anticipation of the northern hemisphere harvest, demand emerged to stem the decline. In particular Egypt, Iraq and Pakistan have been active buyers in the market," she said.
U.S. winter wheat harvest conditions and spring wheat growing conditions over the next four to eight weeks will be of importance, she said.
The market was also closely watching Australian weather after recent confirmation of an El Nino weather pattern, which suggests Australia will have a dry winter and spring, she said.
Subsequent uncertainty about the Australian crop had helped to underpin prices, she said.
The 19967/97 pool sales were now well advanced. Market movements were likely to affect the 1997/98 pool rather than the 1996/97 pool, she said.
The AWB's equity estimate for the 1997/98 pool remains in a range of A$190.00 to A$200.00 a tonne.
